note: Scripture authority is the 1962 Amharic Bible (UBS; NT revised 2003). Its New Testament is on disk whole in the ebible mirror (gracious-tech/fetch_collection, bibles/amh_amh/usfm/; re-verified for this job 2026-10-09: mat and 2co return 200, psa and isa 404). The mirror carries no Old Testament, so OT quotations reuse the wording of an already-shipped Amharic work where one quotes the same verse (source_file names it) and are otherwise self_rendered in the 1962 register.

A `mined` row was re-measured against the finished text: an exact substring of at least 20 characters of the 1962 NT verse (or 25 of the cited corpus file) inside that block. Shorter, re-personed or partly composed quotations are self_rendered.

The English epigraphs are simplified child paraphrases ("— from Psalm 103"); as in the shipped am children's editions (samuel-ajayi-crowther-a-life-children.am) each quotes the Bible's own wording for the part the English means and cites `— ከ<Book> <chapter>`. So chapter 1 says «ለሚፈሩት» (those who fear him) where the child English says "those who love him". Proverbs 17:17a matches rooted-5.am.json's words but is under the 25-character bar (and that file closes the clause with ፤), so it stays self_rendered. Joshua 1:9 reuses women-who-moved-heaven-2.am.json's clause but adds «ጽና፥ አይዞህ» for the English "Be strong and of good courage", so it is self_rendered. Psalm 27:10, 73:26, 82:4 and 30:5 have no shipped Amharic rendering; 73:26 borrows on-loving-god.am.json's opening «ሥጋዬና ልቤ አለቁ» but that file re-persons the rest. Chapter 11's Psalm 103:4 phrase follows the-fourfold-gospel.am.json's «ሕይወትህን ከጥፋት ይቤዣል» turned into a participle, so it is self_rendered.

Conventions: names and places follow the am plan note on family-devotions-brave-and-faithful and author_bios_am/mary-slessor (ሜሪ ስሌሰር, ካላባር, ኤፊክ, ኦኮዮንግ, ዳንዲ, አበርዲን, ጄኒ, ናይጄሪያ, ስኮትላንድ, መንታ); «Everybody's Mother» is «የሁሉም እናት» as in her am short bio. Clock times use Ethiopian reckoning as the am corpus does (6 a.m.–6 p.m. = ከጠዋቱ 12 ሰዓት እስከ ምሽቱ 12 ሰዓት). Quotation marks « », nested ‹ ›; reader addressed as አንተ; prayers open «ውድ እግዚአብሔር ሆይ፣». Each chapter's three study_questions are translated, as the plan card promises.
